brief.headline: Push price down by 3.0% to match our best supplier and win faster payment — we're paying ₹1.26 Cr extra every year for the same material.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the best price we already pay to Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose.
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹68.45/KG but only ₹66.48/KG to Sayaji — a 3.0% gap. The open market band (₹60–81/kg, typical ₹66–73/kg) shows our target sits right in the normal range. They keep 8.5% of every sale as profit and 11.7% as operating profit — plenty of room to meet our price without hardship.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half the current 30) if they give us the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹87.17 L of our cash freed up by moving to 15-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: They are a big, stable company (₹5995.63 Cr revenue) who keep 8.5% profit on every rupee they sell — so a small price cut won't hurt them. We spend ₹21.21 Cr with them, which is only 0.35% of their sales — we're not a make-or-break customer, so we need the alternate-supplier card to back up our ask. Their debt is low (0.13x) and their health score is middling (C, 55/100) — they're solid enough that a tough conversation won't tip them over, but not so dominant that they can ignore us if we have a credible second source lined up.

evidence.point: We pay them 3.0% more than our cheapest supplier for the same material
evidence.figure: Gap vs best: 3.0%; extra cost ₹1.26 Cr/year

evidence.point: They keep a comfortable profit — 8.5% of sales and 11.7% operating profit
Our spend is small for them — less than half a percent of their revenue
evidence.figure: Our ₹21.21 Cr = 0.35% of their ₹5995.63 Cr revenue

evidence.point: The open market shows our target price (₹66.48/KG) sits in the normal band
They supply 56% of our Dextrose — we're heavily reliant on one source

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch and polyol maker (₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B 62/100) — an established dextrose supplier and a drop-in alternate to Gujarat Ambuja; qualify them to split the volume.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C 53/100) — growing capacity in starch and dextrose; a credible second source to reduce our 56% dependency.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of a global starch leader (₹2898.05 Cr revenue) — pharma-grade dextrose with premium quality systems; more expensive but ultra-reliable if we need a backup for critical batches.

risks: They're our main Dextrose source (56% share, ₹21.21 Cr) — if talks go badly and we haven't qualified an alternate, we're stuck paying their price.
We're only 0.35% of their business — they can afford to lose us, so the price push must be backed by a real plan to move volume to Gulshan or Sanstar.
Their health score is middling (C, 55/100) — not distressed, but not bulletproof either; don't squeeze so hard that we destabilise a key supplier before the second source is up and running.
Faster payment (15 days) frees up ₹87.17 L for us, but only offer it in exchange for the full 3.0% price cut — don't give away the early pay for nothing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to bring your Dextrose price in line with the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji — and in return we'll cut your wait for payment from 30 days to 15.
